business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Charter of Prilled Urea and Potassium Chloride

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romanistic-Germanic tradition with federal statutory primacy and significant cantonal administrative autonomy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China-Switzerland Bilateral Investment Treaty of 1986, as supplemented
Switzerland-India Bilateral Investment Treaty of 1997, in force 2002
China-Switzerland Free Trade Agreement, effective 1 July 2014
EFTA Convention and EFTA free trade partner agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act of 10 October 1997 (Geldwae 'schereigesetz, GwG, SR 955.0) as amended; Swiss Criminal Code, SR 311.0, Articles 305bis and 305ter; FINMA Circular 2024/1 on money laundering and payments; AML Ordinance-FINMA; Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220, Articles 634a, 697i and 758; Swiss Federal Act on Commercial Register, SR 221.411; a central publicly searchable Swiss UBO register has not yet been activated and the existing regime relies on shareholder registers, bearer-share controls and mandatory disclosure of beneficial owners to financial intermediaries, authorities and commercial register office upon request.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (no public UBO register; shareholder lists are private; nominee shareholders and directors are permitted but must disclose the ultimate beneficial owner to Swiss financial intermediaries, the commercial register file and supervisory/legal authorities as required by the GwG and Code of Obligations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport or national identification document of each natural-person director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the origin state, alternatively Swiss Consular Legalization in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct or police clearance certificate for each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal records authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder, including register extract evidencing its own beneficial ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company registrar in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization plus authenticated translation into German, French or Italian if the original is not in a Swiss official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth / source-of-funds declaration for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The account-holding financial institution and the contributing beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification followed by Hague Apostille or Swiss Consular Legalization when submitted from a foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners and major counterparties against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions measures, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU restrictive measures referenced or adopted by Switzerland, PEP databases such as World-Check and Dow Jones, and domestic adverse media sources; any PEP relationship triggers enhanced centralized approval; any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing is reported by the Swiss financial intermediary to the Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland (MROS) within the statutory deadlines of the GwG.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Commercial Register (Zentraler Firmenindex) at https://www.zefix.ch, supplemented by the cantonal Commercial Register Office responsible for the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The firm name must use Latin alphabetic characters; Cyrillic, Chinese ideograms and other non-Latin scripts are not accepted in the commercial register; the name must include a Swiss legal-form suffix such as Aktiengesellschaft/AG, Société Anonyme/SA or Società Anonima/SA; foreign-language names are permitted if not misleading and if submitted with documentation in German, French or Italian; English-only descriptive elements may be accepted as fantasy elements but must not imply a regulated activity; transliteration of foreign proper names must follow the official Latin-alphabet transcription and be consistent across all registration documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may within 30 days of written refusal file a reasoned administrative appeal with the cantonal Commercial Register Office seeking reversal; failing that, an appeal lies with the cantonal administrative court and ultimately with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne. A practical alternative is to revise the proposed name to remove the objectionable token and immediately re-apply through the same cantonal office; existing apostilled UBO and identification documents may be used for the resubmission if still within their 90-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual mailbox address is not a lawful registered office for an Aktiengesellschaft; the company must maintain an actual office within a Swiss municipality from which its administration is conducted. For a non-licensed wholesale fertilizer and potash trading company, a shared business center or serviced office with a local management presence may be accepted, but a bare correspondence-only address with no independent operational substance is not compliant and invites objection by the Commercial Register Office and federal tax authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 3.5% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first operating year for a standard non-licensed wholesale trading company; 12% if nominee directors, a virtual office or service-address-only registered office is used; 30% or higher if any MROS filing, sanctions hit, PEP relationship or material inconsistency in the UBO file is detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register entry fee for new Aktiengesellschaft (Handelsregistereintragung)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Register Office of the selected Swiss canton
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal and cantonal registration tariff for an AG, approximate CHF 380

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt / SHAB)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank blocking confirmation for the fully paid minimum capital (Sperrbestätigung / capital verification)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark flat fee or USD 250-350 per hour

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO, SR 220), Arts. 620–643 (founding, registration, legal personality), Art. 632 (paid-up capital), Art. 627 (articles of association); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411); Civil status and company identification rules of the Federal Act on Registration of Enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) acting through the federal e-zefix / EasyGov electronic filing portal; notarial public act required before a Zug notary
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public notarial deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) with the Articles of Association (Statuten) appended, filed as an electronic application for registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) against the commercial register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000 (Art. 621 OR); at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash before registration (Art. 632 para. 2 OR); the paid-up funds must be deposited in a blocked 'i.G.' (in formation) escrow account with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank and may be released to the company only after entry in the commercial register
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously at the first board meeting THAT: (1) the deed of incorporation and the Articles of Association, fixing the share capital at CHF 100,000 divided into 100,000 registered shares of CHF 1.00 each, are adopted; (2) 50,000 shares are subscribed by the founders and fully paid-up by cash deposit in a blocked Swiss bank account 'i.G.'; (3) the funds may be released only upon commercial-register entry; (4) the registered office is fixed at [street address], 6300 Zug, Canton Zug; (5) [Name] is appointed Chairman with individual signature and [Name] as Managing Director with two-by-two collective signature; (6) the notary is instructed to file the registration return with the Zug Commercial Register and to arrange publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug public notary in cooperation with the Zefix/e-zefix name index of the Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed corporate name against the Zefix database to confirm distinctiveness and absence of conflicting prior rights; instruct a Zug notary public; draft the Articles of Association in accordance with Art. 627 OR (name, seat, purpose, share capital, share categories, and organs); convene the founders to execute the public act; obtain specimen signatures of the directors and managing director; ensure at least one authorized signatory resides in Switzerland.
required_dossiers: Zefix name availability confirmation
Draft Articles of Association per Art. 627 OR
Valid passport/ID or commercial register extract of each founder
Confirmation of seat address in the Canton of Zug
Specimen signatures of all board members and the managing director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, a new name motion must be filed via the notary before the public deed is finalized; if the deed is queried, the notary issues a corrective protocol within 30 days of the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Liberation of share capital on a blocked escrow bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank, UBS Switzerland AG) operating a branch in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of 'Aktiengesellschaft i.G.' using the notarized deed and draft articles; deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash with the payment purpose 'liberation of share capital'; obtain the bank's escrow confirmation that the funds are freely disposable by the board only after registration; deliver the confirmation to the notary for attachment to the registration return.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Copy of the draft Articles of Association
AML/KYC identification of all beneficial owners
Credit instruction referencing 'Share capital release / Grundkapital'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes an AML hold, reopen the escrow at another FINMA-supervised bank and supply a substitute escrow certificate; the registry accepts any licensed Swiss bank confirmation evidencing a fully paid-up balance of at least CHF 50,000.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration filing with the Commercial Register of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (via e-zefix / EasyGov authenticated with the notary's digital signature)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration return (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) together with the notarized public act, the bank's capital certificate, and the board's specimen signatures; the registrar verifies capital liberation, legally required organs, seat, purpose, and directors' Swiss residence; confirm the shareholders' waiver of the limited audit under Art. 727a CO if applicable; upon entry the company acquires legal personality (Art. 643 OR); the registry automatically triggers SHAB publication.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed and Articles of Association
Bank certificate evidencing paid-up capital of CHF 50,000
Declaration of residence of all board members
Shareholders' waiver of limited audit (Art. 727a OR) or auditor's consent
Specimen signatures of all authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registrar's deficiency notices within 30 days; if the entry is formally refused, request a written refusal decision (Eintragungsverfügung) and appeal to the Administrative Court of the Canton of Zug within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax base registration and VAT enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration ESTV/FTA (VAT Division); Tax Administration of the Canton of Zug; UID Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon commercial-register entry the Federal Statistical Office issues the company identification number (UID) ex officio; within 30 days of expected turnover exceeding CHF 100,000 in any twelve-month period, file VAT registration (Art. 10 VAT Act, SR 641.20) using the electronic form; file the corporate income tax registration questionnaire with the Zug Tax Administration and the municipality of the registered office; obtain the VAT number for customs and intra-community trade.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract (Zefix)
UID allocation notification
VAT registration application (e-form 101)
Corporate tax registration data sheet of Canton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct and resubmit the VAT application online; if the tax administration queries the registration, provide supplementary explanations and revised turnover projections within 60 days; appeal to the Federal Tax Court against negative VAT decisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB publication, employer onboarding and final governance close-out
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB); Canton Zug social insurance compensation office; SUVA or licensed private accident insurer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SHAB publication of the registered entry; within 60 days of hiring staff, register the company as an employer with the family compensation fund and the statutory accident insurer; adopt the board organizational regulations; verify that the trade is unlicensed under the Cantonal Trade Law but that fertilizer product types are notified to FOAG and any physical storage site obtains the building- and fire-use permit required by the Canton of Zug.
required_dossiers: SHAB publication extract
Employer registration form (AHV/Ausgleichskasse Zug)
Fire-safety certificate for the storage site
Building inspection / structural-load report for bulk silo storage (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For missing storage-site certificates, apply to the Zug building inspectorate for a temporary operating permit with an abatement schedule; payroll registration deficiencies are cured by backdated registration and payment of any late-filing surcharge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG/BLW) – Fertiliser Section, and the Canton of Zug Directorate for Public Works (Baudirektion) for the physical storage facility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Market-placement notification and admission of fertilizer types under the Swiss Fertiliser Ordinance (DüngV, SR 916.171.1): 'Prilled urea (CH4N2O) and potassium chloride (KCl/K2O) categories'; supplemented by a cantonal operating and building-use permit for the warehouse/silo site

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the Zug Environmental Department (Amt für Umweltschutz)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Exempt-to-Registration: wholesale distribution without production does not require a full EIA under the EIA Ordinance (UVPV, SR 814.011, Annex 1); a preliminary EIA screening becomes mandatory if solid fertilizer storage exceeds 10,000 t (UVPV Annex 2, pos. 60.50), otherwise only a building permit with soil, groundwater and drainage conditions is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: no process water release from fertilizer storage; any yard runoff must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201, Annex 3.2), total mineral nitrogen ≤ 10 mg/l as a 24-h average. Air: ammonia and particulates from silo ventilation ≤ 20 mg/m³ and ≤ 10 mg/m³ respectively (Clean Air Ordinance LRV, SR 814.318.142.1, Annex 3); no hazardous VOC threshold applies to prilled urea or potassium chloride. Waste: screening and packaging residues disposed of under the Waste Ordinance (SR 814.600) with documented manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: VKF-recognized fire safety clearance for the storage building including electrical and extinguishing-system approvals; structural load inspection certificate for silo foundations and shelving; SUVA occupational health clearance for dust and ammonia exposure, provision of first-aid facilities, and assessment of the civil-defense shelter obligation based on headcount at the Zug site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Berne; online portal at estv.admin.ch; cantonal tax authorities for federal, cantonal and communal direct tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign AG must first obtain a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) via registration in the Commercial Register through Zefix if it establishes a branch or registered office, or otherwise by direct UID assignment from ESTV. VAT registration is then effected electronically via ESTV e-Services; the ESTV issues a separate MWST-Nr/VAT number. A non-resident AG without a Swiss address must appoint a domestic fiscal representative/domicile before filing. Registration must be completed prior to the first taxable supply in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Swiss AG is a separate taxpayer subject to federal, cantonal and communal income tax; foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate are exempt with progression; not treated as a pass-through entity)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election in Swiss domestic law. Available elections include VAT group treatment for Swiss VAT purposes (Art. 21 VAT Act), participation deduction election for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income, cantonal capital-tax relief elections, and branch VAT-identification election; OECD anti-hybrid rules apply via the Multilateral Instrument and domestic implementing provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT; Mehrwertsteuer / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover in Switzerland (Art. 10 VAT Act); non-established foreign suppliers are generally required to register for VAT when making non-exempt supplies in Switzerland even if below this threshold, unless reverse charge or export zero-rating applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance or digital stamping in Switzerland. Swiss VAT law prescribes statutory invoice content; payment slips referencing Swiss bank accounts must use the Swiss QR-Bill with QR code and creditor reference. eBill and electronic archiving are permitted; tax-relevant invoices must be retained for ten years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (i) goods physically transported from Switzerland to a foreign territory where the export condition is evidenced by customs export documentation; (ii) transport services directly connected to exported goods; and (iii) services for B2B foreign recipients performed outside Switzerland or otherwise used and exploited outside Switzerland under the benefit-abroad rule. For prilled urea and potassium chloride wholesale charter, the exporter must hold valid export proof, commercial documentation, and evidence of physical movement out of Swiss customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic Swiss Export Declaration via NCTS/customs system)
Commercial invoice and export contract with agreed INCOTERMS (e.g., CIF/FOB)
Original Bill of Lading (negotiable maritime B/L) or CMR/Air Waybill for alternative transport
Proof of export to third-country territory (Ausfuhrbescheinigung / customs export certificate)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign sales proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss Federal Tax Administration and customs authorities may apply retrospective scrutiny to export zero-rating. Incomplete or fraudulent proof causes the 0% rate to be reversed, with 8.1% VAT assessed plus default interest from the supply date. Negligent evasion may incur fines of up to three times the tax evaded; intentional evasion or unlawful obtaining of zero-rating/refunds is criminally penalised under Articles 104, 180 and 183 VAT Act, including imprisonment sanctions. Customs false declarations attract separate penalties, and the assessment limitation period for tax evasion is ten years, allowing long look-back clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) — Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca Nazionale Svizzera, statutory monetary authority under the National Bank Act of 3 October 2003 (NBA; SR 951.11), acting in coordination with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for financial-market policy and with SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) for dual-use and trade export controls. Switzerland maintains no separate foreign-exchange-control administration; the SNB is the competent authority for balance-of-payments statistics, foreign-exchange monitoring and prudential FX position reporting of resident banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account. Switzerland observes IMF Article VIII and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements; there are no exchange permits, no quantitative convertibility limits, no prior-authorisation duties for cross-border transfers, and no profit-remittance barriers. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft may freely distribute dividends, redeem share capital and repatriate proceeds, subject only to the statutory 35% anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) which is withheld at source and refunded or reduced under Switzerland's comprehensive double-tax-treaty network. The only practical constraints are (i) the withholding mechanism itself, (ii) SNB statistical reporting thresholds for international transactions, and (iii) the post-negative-rate monetary environment: since June 2022 the SNB policy rate has normalised to a positive range (approximately 1.25%-1.75% as of 2025), restoring conventional CHF treasury optimisation. No capital controls, investment-screening restrictions or current-account barriers apply to a Swiss AG engaged in wholesale fertilizer distribution, including with non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio and no repatriation deadline. All proceeds from physical exports of prilled urea and potassium chloride may be retained in USD, EUR or any freely convertible currency, onshore or offshore, without SNB consent or conversion into CHF. The only mandatory layer is statistical: under the National Bank Statistics Ordinance (SR 951.51), resident exporters must report cross-border receipts through their Swiss clearing bank where aggregated flows exceed the prescribed reporting thresholds, and banks must disclose to the SNB any client FX open position above CHF 3 million per counterparty. Swiss banks may, under their own internal credit policy, require provisioning for export receivables outstanding beyond 240-360 days under IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss rules, but this is a prudential accounting rule, not a statutory surrender or conversion obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency operational account (CHF/EUR/USD) and Capital Escrow Account (Kapitaleinzahlungskonto)
Operational corporate account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque de Commerce et de Placements SA (BCP, Geneva)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Commodity trade-finance operational account with LC and guarantee facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW (2/5) for using a foreign EU/UK electronic-money institution (EMI) as the primary treasury bank of the Swiss AG; MEDIUM (3/5) as an ancillary payment corridor. A non-Swiss EMI cannot passport its electronic-money licence into Switzerland; serving a Swiss resident company from abroad for deposit-taking or payment-account services requires a FINMA licence, a Swiss branch licence, or a permitted outsourcing arrangement under the Swiss Banking Act and the Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FMIA). A FINMA-licensed Swiss fintech (for example, Sonar or Yapeal-type licensed entities) can offer multi-currency virtual IBANs, but tier-1 Swiss banks remain mandatory for USD clearing, documentary credit issuance, standby letters of credit and commodity trade liquidity. Legal caveat: holding trade proceeds or conducting LC settlement through an unlicensed foreign EMI creates regulatory non-transparency and elevated anti-money-laundering risk under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA); such rails are therefore strictly complementary, never structural.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks apply a strict identification and beneficial-ownership duty under AMLA and FINMA Circular 2020/01. For a Swiss AG with non-resident directors and UBOs engaged in agro-chemical commodity wholesaling (banking AML risk tier = Medium_Risk_Enhanced), the baseline standard is: (i) FINMA-recognised video identification with live interview, combined with certified passport copies, may generally satisfy the identity mandate; (ii) nevertheless, most tier-1 banks require at least one physical appearance at the Swiss branch or at a FINMA-recognised foreign correspondent where any director or UBO resides in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction, where the trade chain touches UN/EU/OFAC-sanctioned states, or where the company is newly incorporated and lacks an operating history; and (iii) the bank mandates a notarised and partially apostilled passport, a commercial-register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) issued within six months, a board resolution designating account signatories and confirming the UBO declaration, and a sworn source-of-funds statement. The provision of a complete documentation bundle and a transparent ownership chain will usually permit remote video-based KYC without mandatory physical appearance, but personal appearance becomes effectively compulsory if the enhanced-risk triggers listed above are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-opacity red flag: multi-leg charter routing, ship-to-ship transfers, flags of convenience and mismatched bills of lading in fertilizer cargo flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full trade documentation bundle: (i) the complete chain of charter parties with IMO vessel identification numbers; (ii) original or certified bills of lading and mate's receipts; (iii) independent inspection certificates from SGS, Intertek or GeoChem covering quantity, moisture content and prill-size; (iv) vessel AIS tracking logs and port-state control records; (v) the underlying sale contract with Incoterms and payment schedule; and (vi) a written trade-pattern memorandum validated by the bank's trade-finance desk confirming consistency among counterparties, cargo, freight and payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use / explosive-precursor concern: high-nitrogen urea and ammonium-nitrate-derived products may be diverted to explosives; SECO dual-use export controls may apply.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit product specifications confirming standard agricultural-prilled-urea grade (>46% N), a SECO dual-use export-control assessment or licence where the destination falls outside domestic fertiliser-use scope, end-user and end-use certificates from registered agro-industrial purchasers, ADR/IMDG transport certification for dangerous goods, Swiss customs entries (NACBS e-dec) evidencing lawful import-export, and a destination-control clause incorporated in each sales confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership through nominee structures, bearer-share-like arrangements, or multi-layer holding companies obscuring the natural persons behind the Swiss AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) the Swiss commercial-register extract including the share-register position; (ii) an AMLA-compliant UBO declaration (Art. 4 GwG) naming every individual with more than a 10% economic interest; (iii) apostilled or FINMA-accepted passport copies of all directors and UBOs; (iv) a look-through legal-structure chart ending at natural persons; and (v) an irrevocable written undertaking to notify the bank within ten business days of any ownership change at or above the 10% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-corridor risk: fertilizer transactions routed via third-country trading houses in jurisdictions subject to Swiss, UN, EU or OFAC measures, particularly for urea or potash of Russian or Belarusian origin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce counterparty KYC packages, certificates of origin (e.g., Canada, China, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Egypt), non-circumvention declarations, evidence that payment chains exclude sanctioned banks and sanctioned currencies, and — where a permitted exception applies — the relevant SECO licence or Federal Council authorisation. Additionally, maintain a continuous sanctions-screening ledger for all counterparties against the consolidated Swiss SECO sanctions lists, and provide it to the bank on request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structured prepayment or pre-financing to third-country suppliers that may be mischaracterised as trade-based money laundering or unlicensed lending activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the underlying purchase contract and commercial invoices, the bank-confirmed letter of credit or documentary-collection instructions, an advance-payment schedule tied to discrete shipment milestones, a cash-flow projection and audited financial statements evidencing economic capacity, and — where applicable — a standby letter of credit or bank guarantee posted on behalf of the seller. All advances must reconcile precisely with the trade-finance credit line established at the servicing Swiss bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for inbound equity injections into the Swiss AG: (1) The foreign shareholder instructs a SWIFT MT103 transfer to the Swiss account bank with the beneficiary named exactly as CH_AG, the remitter exactly matching the shareholder of record, and the SNB balance-of-payments statistical purpose code for direct-investment capital contribution (Kapitalzufuhr / apport de capital) stated in field 70 or 77B. (2) Funds are credited to the dedicated Capital Escrow Account (Kapitaleinzahlungskonto) opened in the company's name; the bank then issues the capital-contribution confirmation (Liberierungsbestatigung) required for notarial filing under Articles 629 ff. of the Swiss Code of Obligations. (3) The minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 must be fully paid in cash, or in-kind contributions must be documented by a statutory audit report. (4) No SNB or FINMA prior authorisation is required, but the receiving Swiss bank must record the payment for national balance-of-payments statistics and monthly SNB reporting; relevant clearing rails are SIC for CHF, EuroSIC/SEPA for EUR and CHIPS/Fedwire for USD through tier-1 correspondent relationships. (5) After the commercial-register registration certificate is delivered, the escrowed balance may be reclassified to the operational trading account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound physical fertilizer trade settlements: (a) SWIFT MT103 irrevocable wire transfers for cash-against-documents, freight, demurrage and ancillary trade payments, each carrying the correct Swiss balance-of-payments purpose code and referencing the underlying invoice, contract or charter-party number. (b) Commercial documentary letters of credit issued through the Swiss advising bank via SWIFT MT700 and amendments via MT707 under UCP600, with clauses requiring loading-port inspection certificates (SGS, Intertek or equivalent), weight and quality analysis, certificate of origin, phyto-sanitary certification where applicable, and vessel-age and ISM-code compliance. (c) Standby letters of credit under URDG 758 or ISP98 issued via SWIFT MT760 to secure charter-party obligations, performance bonds and demurrage/despatch settlements. (d) Bank guarantees for port operations and customs bonds, collateralised by the AG's own deposits or treasury lines. (e) For African and Asian procurement corridors, documentary collections (DP/DA) with SWIFT MT202 cover and reimbursement authorisations may be used, provided each disbursement is captured by the SNB statistical reporting and the bank's sanctions-and-AML screening engine.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CHF/USD and CHF/EUR foreign-exchange forwards (Devisentermingeschaefte) documented under an ISDA 2002 Swiss Schedule or a Swiss Master Agreement for the physical settlement of urea and potash purchase and sale flows
Foreign-exchange swaps (FX swaps) for rolling short-term treasury cover of import-payable and export-receipt maturity mismatches

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with a USD deliverable leg for procurement in restricted-currency corridors (e.g., INR, EGP, NGN, UAH) where the local interbank forward market is operationally inaccessible
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) converting syndicated USD trade finance into CHF or EUR funding on an amortising schedule matched to cargo delivery cycles
Plain-vanilla FX options, collars and participating forwards for protection of export-receipt conversion budgets, executed OTC with a licensed Swiss bank as counterparty
SARON vs SOFR and SARON vs EURIBOR cross-currency basis swaps aligning CHF/EUR treasury positions with dollar-denominated commodity purchase contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting and Adoption of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders as corporate organ; no public filing; minutes kept in corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of balance sheet date per Art. 699 para. 2 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure to convene the AGM triggers a compliance deadline from the Commercial Register authority; continued default permits court-ordered dissolution on shareholder application; directors face fines up to CHF 5,000 and personal civil liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined Cantonal and Federal Direct Tax Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered seat (Amt für Steuern Zug) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing; Zug statutory deadline for legal entities is 31 March, with routine administrative extension to 30 September of the following tax year; one combined form for cantonal and federal direct tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 3.5% per annum on unpaid tax; late-filing fine up to CHF 10,000 per Art. 175 DBG; intentional evasion surcharge of up to 1.5 times the evaded tax plus criminal prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Value Added Tax Return (quarterly remittance cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 60 days after each calendar quarter-end; an annual VAT return is permitted only where annual turnover is below CHF 500,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 4% per annum; administrative fine up to CHF 8,000 per Art. 72 of the Swiss VAT Act; suspension of VAT number for persistent non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Integrity Review of Share Register and Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal board and registered office agent; registers accessible to the Commercial Register Office and tax authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing duty; formal verification by the board at each annual accounts meeting; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership recorded within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or incomplete book entries constitute criminal misrepresentation under Arts. 152-153 of the Swiss Criminal Code; additional fines under the Federal Transparency of Legal Entities Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Update Filing (event-driven; no recurring annual filing exists for Swiss AGs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canton Zug Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of a registrable event (change of director, registered office, share capital, statutory representative) per Art. 10 of the Commercial Register Ordinance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 5,000 per default; continued omission of mandatory entries may lead to official strike-off and dissolution proceedings by the register authority

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audit Report (Limited or Ordinary Revision) for Annual General Meeting Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent licensed audit firm; report submitted to shareholders; not publicly filed for non-listed stock corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit completed before the AGM; financial statements must be finalized no later than 6 months after the balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a required audit opinion prevents lawful AGM approval; board liability for presenting unaudited accounts; register authority may impose compliance deadlines and fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is mandatory if two of three criteria are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, or more than 250 full-time employees on annual average; listed companies are always subject to ordinary audit. All other AGs require a limited audit, except that a company with fewer than 10 full-time employees may dispense with any audit upon unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory accounting rules of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Arts. 957-963b); Swiss GAAP FER permitted and commonly adopted for medium-sized entities; IFRS not mandatory absent a stock exchange listing or qualified financial institution status

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland imposes no separate annual public UBO confirmation filing. Under the Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities, the AG must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners at its registered office, update it within 30 days of any ownership change, and disclose it to competent authorities upon request; share transfers are recorded in the share register (Aktienbuch), where registered shares must be endorsed and the acquirer revealed to the company before voting rights are exercised.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch) including beneficial owner annotations
Register of Directors and Auditors (Verzeichnis der Mitglieder des Verwaltungsrates und der Revisionsstelle)
Minute Book of Annual General Meeting and Board Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% direct federal corporate income tax imposed on after-tax profit, combined with Zug cantonal and communal taxes to produce a combined effective headline rate of approximately 11.9% of commercial pre-tax operating profit for the 2023/2024 assessment cycle.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland grants no statutory general tax holiday. The effective rate is reduced by: (1) the participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains from shareholdings of at least 10% held continuously for 12 months; (2) the Zug patent or IP box regime granting up to a 90% exemption of qualifying net intellectual property income, applicable only where the wholesale supply process embeds patented logistics or product technology; (3) an additional research and development super-deduction of 50% of qualifying R&D expenditure for companies performing R&D in Switzerland; (4) the Notional Interest Deduction on excess qualifying equity available in the Canton of Zug; and (5) moderate cantonal capital tax. Loss carryforwards of up to 7 years were introduced by the 2020 OASI Financing Act reform.
